title: Compare wrapping packet sequences
description: Implement int sequence_is_newer(uint16_t candidate, uint16_t previous).
prompt:
Implement int sequence_is_newer(uint16_t candidate, uint16_t previous).
Return 1 exactly when the forward modular distance from previous to candidate is in [1, 32767]. Equal values and the ambiguous half-range distance 32768 return 0.
constraints: Use unsigned arithmetic; do not rely on narrowing to a signed type.

tests.name: Next packet
Equal packet
Wrap forward
Old packet
Ambiguous half range

reference_solution.solution.c:
#include <stdint.h>
int sequence_is_newer(uint16_t candidate, uint16_t previous) { uint16_t d=(uint16_t)((uint32_t)candidate + 65536u - previous); return d != 0 && d < 32768u; }

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: Which boundary conditions would you test on the target?
What changes if the function is called from an ISR?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
